text:
sam_infra: FYI seeing pod connections drop intermittently in westus2 gpupool, lots of 5xx from model-serving frontends
lee_sre: seen an alert earlier — conntrack high on the nodes serving that pool?
maria_platform: looking at node metrics now, conntrack table at ~380k entries on node-gpu-12 (nf_conntrack_max is 393216)
sam_infra: that explains the drops — once it hits max new connections get DROP/REJECT
jordan_runtime: any idea what is creating so many ephemeral flows? workload hasn't changed much
sam_infra: traffic patterns show lots of short lived s->s east-west chat calls and model shard prefetching, plus periodic health-check fanout
lee_sre: running quick checks: `ssh node-gpu-12 sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` -> 380112
lee_sre: `ss -s` shows many TIME_WAIT/ESTAB sockets; `iptables -t nat -L` shows kube-proxy MASQUERADE rules in place
maria_platform: also noticed heavy RDMA RDMA-enabled pods — when MTU mismatches occur we get retransmits and more connection churn
ops-bot: incident_bot: high_conntrack_count detected on node-gpu-12 (380k) — paging oncall
sam_infra: immediate mitigation: reduce nf_conntrack_max? risky but buys headroom. Thoughts?
lee_sre: we can temporarily bump `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288` on affected nodes, but long-term we need root cause
jordan_runtime: rolling that on ~10 nodes now via ad-hoc DaemonSet (one-off) — will watch for memory pressure
maria_platform: opened tcpdump on pod sidecar. Saw a storm of short 1-2 packet connections to internal redis/rendezvous every 2s
sam_infra: maybe our prefetcher is opening new TCP connections instead of reusing keep-alive; causes conntrack churn
lee_sre: also found many conntrack entries in CLOSE_WAIT with no timeout clearing — kernel conntrack timeouts look elevated for CLOSE states
lee_sre: `conntrack -L | grep CLOSE_WAIT | wc -l` -> 102k
maria_platform: workaround: lower `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close_wait` from default (usually 60s) to 10s for these nodes
jordan_runtime: applied both: bumped max and reduced close_wait timeout on the hot nodes. conntrack count dropped ~30k in 2m
sam_infra: nice. still seeing some packet loss for large payloads — could be MTU/RDMA interplay
lee_sre: checked `dmesg` on node-gpu-12: repeated "TCP: Possible reordering" and "device eth0: msg lost" entries; switching to jumbo MTU not trivial for whole AZ
maria_platform: short-term: pin pods that use RDMA to nodes with consistent MTU and disable packetization offload? we can try `ethtool -K eth0 tx off` on a test node
jordan_runtime: test applied to one node -> model-serving p95 latency improved and retransmits dropped
sam_infra: action items:
- (sam_infra) roll a targeted DaemonSet to bump nf_conntrack_max to 524288 for gpupool nodes (ttl 24h) and reduce close_wait timeout
- (jordan_runtime) patch prefetcher to reuse TCP connections / enable HTTP keep-alive
- (maria_platform) create node affinity for RDMA-heavy pods to MTU-homogenous nodes
- (lee_sre) add conntrack eviction monitoring and automated sweep alert (conntrack > 70%)
- (all) assess long-term: implement node-local DNS/NAT or service mesh sidecar connection pooling
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling update started for daemonset/conntrack-boost
sam_infra: note for postmortem: cost impact of bumped conntrack_max (kernel memory) and risk of not addressing app-level churn
maria_platform: added follow-up ticket in infra backlog #INFRA-462 to schedule MTU remediation window
lee_sre: will capture `conntrack -S` and `ss -tanp` snapshot and attach to ticket
jordan_runtime: thanks, monitoring now shows recovery. will keep watching for 30m and then revert temporary sysctl if stable :thumbsup:
sam_infra: thanks all, keep thread updated if anything regresses
